sentences.text:
Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:47532
Court No. - 76
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 39195 of 2023

Applicant :- Sudhir @ Golu
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

Counsel for Applicant :- A.K. Mishra,Mamta Singh,Mohd Haider
Counsel for Opposite Party :- Ajay Singh Sengar,G.A.,Vijay Singh Sengar
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.

Heard Ms. Mamta Singh, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Ajay Singh Sengar, learned counsel
for the informant and Sri Pradeep Kumar, learned Aga for the State-respondent.

2.  The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.
503 of 2023, under Sections 363, 507, 376-D, 384 IPC, Police Station- Kotwali Nagar, District- Bulandshahar, during pendency of the trial in the court below.

3. FIR of the present case was lodged against unknown person and according to the FIR, marriage of the informant was performed with the prosecutrix about 12 years before and he was having some doubt on the character of his wife and his wife left his house with her paramour and from her matrimonial home, she has taken Rs. 20,000/- and golden jewelleries.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that entire allegation made against the applicant is totally false and applicant never committed rape upon the victim i.e. wife of the informant and actually it appears that victim, who is married lady, developed illicit relationship with the applicant Sudhir @ Golu vs State Of U.P. on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72625988/
1 and when her husband came to know about this fact then she left her matrimonial home but after recovery, she started making allegation of rape against the applicant and the fact that she was having illicit relationship with the applicant is evident from her statements recorded under Sections 161 Cr.P.C. and 164 Cr.P.C.
5.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: She further submitted that there are material contradictions in both the statements of the victim recorded during investigation and in her statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. she made allegation of rape against applicant and others but in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. she made allegation of rape only against the applicant.

6. She further submitted that after considering entire facts of the case co-accused Naveen Kumar has been released on bail by this Court and as far as allegation of rape made in the statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C. is concerned, case of applicant is at par with co-accused Naveen Kumar.

7. She further submitted that applicant is not having any criminal history and he is in jail since 02.07.2023.
8.

Per contra, learned AGA as well as learned counsel for the informant opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that victim categorically in her both the statements recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. and 164 Cr.P.C. stated that applicant committed rape upon her and, therefore, his case is distinguishable from the case of co-accused Naveen Kumar and, therefore, considering the nature of allegation and statements of the victim recorded during investigation, applicant should not be released on bail.
9.
I have heard both the parties and perused the record of the case.

10. However, victim in her both the statements recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. and 164 Cr.P.C.
made allegation of rape and sexual assault against the applicant but she is major and married lady and from her both the statements, it appears that she was having illicit relationship with the applicant.

11. Further, argument advanced by learned counsel for the applicant that victim was having illicit relationship with the applicant and when her husband came to know about this fact then under his pressure, she started making allegation of rape against the applicant, cannot be completely ruled out.
12. Further, co-accused Naveen Kumar has been released on bail by this Court, however, after perusing the statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 Cr.PC.

it appear that his case is distinguishable from the applicant but considering the statement of the victim recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C., it appears that case of applicant is at par with co-accused Navven Kumar.
13. Further, applicant is not having any criminal history and he is in jail since July, 2023.

sentences.text: Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
15. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

16. Let the applicant- Sudhir @ Golu be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
17.
In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

18. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
